=== connection-skill-per-connection-type.md ===
---
name: connection-skill-per-connection-type
description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's chosen proposal for how the agent gets better printer knowledge over time: one connection skill per connection type, added when a person connects, driven by honest tool states, grown by reviewed PRs and opt-in reports. Recorded, not implemented."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 73de5d33-07b2-44a6-bbd2-bedca734a244
  modified: 2026-11-02T20:40:31.571Z
---

Kenneth confirmed this on 2026-11-02 (in a forked side session, "AI agent design for printer setup") as the one to try for the open problem in the P1S handoff: how the agent gets correct printer and connection knowledge when the team cannot test most printers.

Update, later on 2026-11-02: built for Bambu. "The one right next step for each" in point 2 below was a rewording, and the state-to-step table it produced failed on the real P1S. The skill now explains how the connection works: see [[connection-skill-explains-not-lookup]]. Print hosts have no skill yet, and the person-corrected-the-model report trigger is not built.

1. **When:** the moment a person tries to connect a printer in the chat, the app adds one skill to that conversation. Not before, and not for people who only pick a profile and prepare prints.
2. **What:** a text file in the repo, one per connection type (Bambu first, then Moonraker/OctoPrint), chosen by the app from the connection type, never by the model. It holds the procedure: which tool to call, what each reported state means, and the one right next step for each, including silence, where it tells the model to ask what the person sees and wait rather than conclude. It holds no menu wording the app cannot verify.
3. **Tools:** the status and connect tools report the situation exactly as the app observes it (heard nothing yet, port taken, plug-in missing, cloud mode, wrong code, the host's own refusal reason). The skill drives the conversation from those states; the tools never carry the procedure.
4. **Improvement loop:** the skill grows by pull request reviewed by a person, like OrcaSlicer's profiles. When the agent and the person are struggling, by a rule the app applies (a connect attempt failed twice, or the person corrected the model), the chat asks whether to send a report to the JusPrin developers. The person sees what will be sent and says yes or no; nothing is sent otherwise. The report holds the tool states and the connection turns, never the access code or API key, and goes to our server directly so people on their own API keys can send it too.
5. **Evidence rule:** before any skill line is written for a state, that state must have been made to happen for real. The Bambu side has mostly done this; the host side only for Moonraker and OctoPrint.

**Why:** it replaces three earlier ideas Kenneth rejected: steps in the standing prompt, a "file per printer model" that was invented jargon and the wrong key for Klipper hosts, and counting data points, which OrcaSlicer never does. Connection type is the key the code already has.

**How to apply:** when work on printer-connection guidance starts, build this, not a variant; check each state against [[p1s-connect-incident-2026-10-31]] and [[tool-result-states-method]] (Kenneth's test for what counts as a problem). Open as of 2026-11-02: Bambu plug-in code -1 on a wrong access code, never 5; whether -1 is a rejection or a timeout.

=== connection-skill-explains-not-lookup.md ===
---
name: connection-skill-explains-not-lookup
description: "Kenneth 2026-11-02: judge a skill by whether the agent guides a stuck person and makes educated guesses; a state-to-step table failed on the real P1S, so the skill explains how the connection works"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: e4ed3f35-35dc-4121-ba7d-12c70a470bf1
  modified: 2026-11-02T20:36:54.235Z
---

On 2026-11-02, after reading live chats where the agent told Kenneth to re-check a correct access code, Kenneth said: "The important thing is if the agent was able to guide the user throughout the process effectively and try to make educated guess... We can't just patch up for this use case. We need a mechanism that can work for most cases." He approved this mechanism:

1. The skill explains how the connection works, step by step, and what tells causes apart. It is not a table of state to next step.
2. The printer prompt holds one way of working: likeliest explanation marked as a guess, cheapest check, drop what is ruled out, never repeat a failed step unless something changed.
3. The app reports what it observed, not conclusions. A failed Bambu note gives the plug-in's code, how long it took, and a TCP look at port 8883 (`look_at_port`). The old note said "refused", which was false.
4. Tests judge where the chat leaves the person (`ended_badly` in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`), including failures the skill was not written from.

**Why:** "one right next step for each" and "wait rather than conclude" were my rewording of his proposal, not his words. His words were a "not so complicated skill file" that guides the user to finish connecting. "Add no cause of your own" was entirely mine, and it made the model repeat a false reason. Green tests hid this because they judged wording and states.

Later the same day I held the commit for about 3 hours to find out why his P1S goes quiet, then asked him to restart it. He said: "The goal here is not to connect my printer." A failing real printer is the test case for the agent's help, so do not repair it, explain it or wait for it before testing.

He also said I keep writing "its line was wrong" for lines I wrote. Say "I wrote it" and say why. My likely reason for "add no cause": a false statement is a failure I could see and test for, and a stuck person was not, so I kept the "false" half of his test and dropped the "a person stuck" half.

**How to apply:** when a chat goes wrong, read what the person was told before touching a line of it. Do not answer with a patch for the failing line; ask what stopped the model reasoning. The evidence rule in [[connection-skill-per-connection-type]] now covers facts the skill states; guesses are allowed when labelled. See [[bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code]], [[tool-result-states-method]], [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].

=== tool-result-states-method.md ===
---
name: tool-result-states-method
description: "2026-11-01/02 tool-result sweep: Kenneth's test for a result bug (a person stuck: told something false, right step hidden, cost beyond one call); how the problem statement drifted into 'every distinguishable state' and eight of nine fixes were taken out; branch claude/tool-results-truth"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b2d2c400-439c-4486-af2f-1479f86f533d
  modified: 2026-11-02T12:51:30.620Z
---

After the P1S cloud-mode incident (2026-10-31) a code-reading sweep listed eleven tools whose result said less than the app knew, and I fixed nine of them on `claude/tool-silent-failures` (common branch `claude/tool-results-truth`). On 2026-11-02 Kenneth asked why, and eight came out again.

**Kenneth's test for a tool-result bug:** a person who plausibly exists, told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call. "Fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem." The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call is not a stuck person. The three that passed: a wrong Bambu access code read as a vanished printer; a print host that answered read as unreachable; a heard printer hidden from the connection (same loop as the incident).

**How the statement drifted:** incident (a person stuck, false reason, right step hidden) → sweep ("a tool says less than the app knew", a code shape, eleven matches by reading) → brief ("a class of bug", method + guard, "reproduce before fixing") → my reading (reproduce = make two states read the same over MCP, a property of the code). Each hand-off made it easier to satisfy. The hidden-preset "fix" was the clearest non-problem: no person, the sweep itself said "may be intended".

**Why:** the P1S failure was real because you were on the wrong side of it for an evening; the other ten shared its code shape, not its substance. Every field added for a non-problem is text every model reads on every call.

**How to apply:** before fixing a result, write the scenario in Kenneth's terms (who, doing what, told what, losing what, which step is hidden); if it cannot be written, it is not a problem, whatever the code looks like. When a brief says "reproduce", ask whether it means "find the case a person hit" (it does, [[reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes]]) before accepting a weaker reading, and raise the gap on receipt, not when asked three times. A rule or guard is worth keeping when it would fail on the real incident; a document nobody reads is not ([[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]] still stands). Kept guards: `test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", harness `*_are_told_apart`, `FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, `StandInHost(hold, answer, status, body)`. Seam: one line in `GUI_App.cpp`'s local-connect CallAfter → `Printers::record_connection_event`; upstream/main added a log line at the same spot, resolve by keeping both.

=== forward-the-real-error-four-rules.md ===
---
name: forward-the-real-error-four-rules
description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's method for false tool results: forward what the source gave, else say what the code tested; no new checks; no OrcaSlicer files; applied to sweep entries 1-43 as 469ecf0f8a and b87ab789ca"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: b47f90f4-7491-4a9c-a16a-eddb38284f24
  modified: 2026-11-02T20:28:22.151Z
---

On 2026-11-02 a sweep listed 71 places where a tool result hid or replaced the real failure. I offered "separate checks" for failures with several causes and said each removed claim "needs a check of what's true". Kenneth called that out: separate checks to tell causes apart are the thing we are trying not to do, and if the code knows nothing, there is nothing to check. He approved four rules for entries 1-43:

1. If the source gives an error, forward it.
2. If it gives nothing, say what the code tested or saw, and delete any guessed cause. No new checks or branches.
3. If a comment says a lower layer's message misleads the model, keep our replacement. Example: `generate_calibration` drops the over-the-build-volume load report on purpose.
4. If the fix needs an OrcaSlicer file, skip the entry. Kenneth approves any upstream change one by one.

He also waived per-entry reproduction for this batch only. It does not replace the global "reproduce before fixing" rule for other bugs.

**Why:** the fix is mechanical once it is seen as forwarding. Inventing a way to classify causes is over-engineering, and it was the earlier reading of "reproduce" that made eight sweep fixes come out again ([[tool-result-states-method]]).

**How to apply:**
- Before proposing work on a tool result, ask what the source already gives. Say "forward" or "delete the claim", and propose no new check.
- A forwarded error reaches the model, so it must not name Orca: `wording.test.ts` does not see those strings. Two throws in `ProjectAutosave.cpp` had to change.
- False successes are the exception, because the source gives nothing to forward: `store_stl` always returns true, `export_current_configs` lists unwritten files, `Plater::split_object` returns nothing and only shows a modal, and `ModelObject::split` on a multi-volume object splits only by volume.
- Before a force-push or squash on `claude/tool-results-truth`, say a push already happened. Kenneth dropped a squash once he heard it needed one. Pushing to origin needs his word, not my note that it is the process.

Left on the list after these commits: entries 44-71, except 47, 48 and 49. Related: [[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]], [[tool-error-contract]].

=== rare-failures-get-a-generic-error.md ===
---
name: rare-failures-get-a-generic-error
description: "Kenneth 2026-10-15 — rare, speculative failure paths (save failures etc.) get one generic error; don't design per-cause handling, retries or prompt rules for them"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ef1c9e7b-9046-4021-b7fe-b659d08d3643
  modified: 2026-10-15T20:51:18.020Z

On 2026-10-15 Kenneth reviewed my nozzle-change proposal. It had per-cause error messages, prompt rules and handling for save failures caused by a full disk, an open paint tool or a not-yet-drawn canvas. He said those cases were wrong, speculative or rare, and that they should simply get a generic error.

**Why:** they are hard to handle well and almost never happen. The effort belongs on failures people actually hit, like the printer panel's action-id collision, which I reproduced.

**How to apply:** before proposing handling for a failure, ask whether a real person will plausibly hit it. If it's rare or unreproduced, recommend the existing generic error and move on. Don't list speculative causes as if they were findings. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[printer-panel-action-id-collision]].

=== printer-setup-connect-means-verify-and-save.md ===
---
name: printer-setup-connect-means-verify-and-save
description: "In printer setup, \"connect your printer\" means discover/enter, verify and save connection details — not keep the connection software active afterward"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 4bc09f89-3c93-41af-a38f-07026451bff6
  modified: 2026-09-23T22:22:45.282Z
---

Kenneth settled this on 2026-09-23. In the printer setup flow, "connect your printer" is user wording. For the code it means: find or enter the printer's connection details, check that they work, and save them with that printer. The check may open a real connection for a moment. Setup does NOT promise that the connection stays active after a later printer-profile change.

**Why:** commit 9f739dccf2 read "connect" as "keep Bambu's connection software selected whatever profile is chosen later". To do that it added an app-wide override to OrcaSlicer's `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent()` (10 upstream lines). The coding agent that wrote it later agreed it had invented that requirement. On jusprin-newui, 264d6f8141 removes the override and bd8ea51abc adds the harness checks. With it gone, selecting a non-Bambu profile gives the connection software back to Orca's profile-driven choice, the same as stock Orca.

**How to apply:**
- Don't add code that keeps a printer connection alive across profile changes unless Kenneth asks for that behavior explicitly.
- After the connection software changes, printer status stays "connected" for up to 30 seconds. That is the normal freshness window in `has_recent_printer_data`, the same one that applies when a printer is switched off. It is not a regression.

Related: [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]], [[printer-conversation-panel-19b]].

=== bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code.md ===
---
name: bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code
description: "Plug-in code -1 on Kenneth's P1S came with the correct access code while the network was very slow; a direct MQTT login separates a wrong code (rc 5) from a right one (rc 0)"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 445726c4-adce-47cb-81a4-658405e48110
  modified: 2026-11-02T20:40:28.093Z
---

2026-11-02, Kenneth's P1S at 192.168.0.198 in LAN mode, plug-in 02.03.00.62. The real access code gave `ConnectStatusFailed` msg `-1` twice, about 24 s after `set_selected_machine`, the same as a made-up code. A one-off MQTT login to port 8883 (user `bblp`, 60 s timeout) answered CONNACK 0 with the real code and CONNACK 5 with a made-up one, so the code was right and the printer does tell them apart. During those failures TCP 8883 timed out for over a minute. An idle ping showed 64% loss and 15-50 s round trips, while the router answered in 3 ms and other Wi-Fi devices on the network were also slow.

Later on 2026-11-02, a saved LAN record at an address with no device at all (TCP 8883: "Host is down") also got `-1`, 12 s after selecting it, and the app's note said "refused". So -1 means at least "no connection made"; it does not need a printer to answer.

Correction, 2026-11-02 12:12: I blamed Kenneth's slow Wi-Fi, and a weak signal now looks unlikely. With no app running, about 3 hours after the last connection attempt from my tests, the printer lost 35% of pings at 9.6 s average while the router answered in 3 ms with no loss, and the printer reported -41 dBm and IDLE. A direct login with the right code was accepted but took 27.7 s, 26 s of it setting up TLS, which is longer than the ~24 s after which the plug-in reports -1. My hypothesis, unverified: on a slow printer the plug-in gives up before the code is tested. The cause of the slowness is unknown. Finding it is not the goal: see [[connection-skill-explains-not-lookup]].

**Why:** the app's note said "The printer refused the connection" until commit 35fed2c439 and its follow-up, and the skill's `failed` line tells the model to have the person compare the code. For this person both were false and hid the real problem. My hypothesis, unverified: -1 is the plug-in's timeout, and on a healthy network a wrong code gives another answer, perhaps the `5` upstream handles.

**How to apply:** before concluding anything from a connect failure, check that the printer answers on TCP 8883 in under a second; `--printer-live-p1s <address> real-code` takes the code from `JUSPRIN_P1S_CODE`. A failure during a slow spell says nothing about the code. See [[printer-network-check-harness]] and [[connection-skill-per-connection-type]].

**Why:** the 2026-10-14 handoff turned "one home per rule" into "the prompt is the home". **How to apply:** ask "who needs this rule?" A rule about one tool's arguments or output goes in its description even if it says "ask" or "explain". Check the host's per-turn lines before calling them a rule's home: the "file-load reports are source data" developer line exists only for files the person opened, not for project_open called by the model or for MCP. Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.

**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.

**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.

**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".

**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). Related: [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[tool-call-approval-removed]].

1	=== connection-skill-per-connection-type.md ===
2	---
3	name: connection-skill-per-connection-type
4	description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's chosen proposal for how the agent gets better printer knowledge over time: one connection skill per connection type, added when a person connects, driven by honest tool states, grown by reviewed PRs and opt-in reports. Recorded, not implemented."
5	metadata:
6	  node_type: memory
7	  type: project
8	  originSessionId: 73de5d33-07b2-44a6-bbd2-bedca734a244
9	  modified: 2026-11-02T20:40:31.571Z
10	---
11	
12	Kenneth confirmed this on 2026-11-02 (in a forked side session, "AI agent design for printer setup") as the one to try for the open problem in the P1S handoff: how the agent gets correct printer and connection knowledge when the team cannot test most printers.
13	
14	Update, later on 2026-11-02: built for Bambu. "The one right next step for each" in point 2 below was a rewording, and the state-to-step table it produced failed on the real P1S. The skill now explains how the connection works: see [[connection-skill-explains-not-lookup]]. Print hosts have no skill yet, and the person-corrected-the-model report trigger is not built.
15	
16	1. **When:** the moment a person tries to connect a printer in the chat, the app adds one skill to that conversation. Not before, and not for people who only pick a profile and prepare prints.
17	2. **What:** a text file in the repo, one per connection type (Bambu first, then Moonraker/OctoPrint), chosen by the app from the connection type, never by the model. It holds the procedure: which tool to call, what each reported state means, and the one right next step for each, including silence, where it tells the model to ask what the person sees and wait rather than conclude. It holds no menu wording the app cannot verify.
18	3. **Tools:** the status and connect tools report the situation exactly as the app observes it (heard nothing yet, port taken, plug-in missing, cloud mode, wrong code, the host's own refusal reason). The skill drives the conversation from those states; the tools never carry the procedure.
19	4. **Improvement loop:** the skill grows by pull request reviewed by a person, like OrcaSlicer's profiles. When the agent and the person are struggling, by a rule the app applies (a connect attempt failed twice, or the person corrected the model), the chat asks whether to send a report to the JusPrin developers. The person sees what will be sent and says yes or no; nothing is sent otherwise. The report holds the tool states and the connection turns, never the access code or API key, and goes to our server directly so people on their own API keys can send it too.
20	5. **Evidence rule:** before any skill line is written for a state, that state must have been made to happen for real. The Bambu side has mostly done this; the host side only for Moonraker and OctoPrint.
21	
22	**Why:** it replaces three earlier ideas Kenneth rejected: steps in the standing prompt, a "file per printer model" that was invented jargon and the wrong key for Klipper hosts, and counting data points, which OrcaSlicer never does. Connection type is the key the code already has.
23	
24	**How to apply:** when work on printer-connection guidance starts, build this, not a variant; check each state against [[p1s-connect-incident-2026-10-31]] and [[tool-result-states-method]] (Kenneth's test for what counts as a problem). Open as of 2026-11-02: Bambu plug-in code -1 on a wrong access code, never 5; whether -1 is a rejection or a timeout.
25	
26	=== connection-skill-explains-not-lookup.md ===
27	---
28	name: connection-skill-explains-not-lookup
29	description: "Kenneth 2026-11-02: judge a skill by whether the agent guides a stuck person and makes educated guesses; a state-to-step table failed on the real P1S, so the skill explains how the connection works"
30	metadata:
31	  node_type: memory
32	  type: feedback
33	  originSessionId: e4ed3f35-35dc-4121-ba7d-12c70a470bf1
34	  modified: 2026-11-02T20:36:54.235Z
35	---
36	
37	On 2026-11-02, after reading live chats where the agent told Kenneth to re-check a correct access code, Kenneth said: "The important thing is if the agent was able to guide the user throughout the process effectively and try to make educated guess... We can't just patch up for this use case. We need a mechanism that can work for most cases." He approved this mechanism:
38	
39	1. The skill explains how the connection works, step by step, and what tells causes apart. It is not a table of state to next step.
40	2. The printer prompt holds one way of working: likeliest explanation marked as a guess, cheapest check, drop what is ruled out, never repeat a failed step unless something changed.
41	3. The app reports what it observed, not conclusions. A failed Bambu note gives the plug-in's code, how long it took, and a TCP look at port 8883 (`look_at_port`). The old note said "refused", which was false.
42	4. Tests judge where the chat leaves the person (`ended_badly` in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`), including failures the skill was not written from.
43	
44	**Why:** "one right next step for each" and "wait rather than conclude" were my rewording of his proposal, not his words. His words were a "not so complicated skill file" that guides the user to finish connecting. "Add no cause of your own" was entirely mine, and it made the model repeat a false reason. Green tests hid this because they judged wording and states.
45	
46	Later the same day I held the commit for about 3 hours to find out why his P1S goes quiet, then asked him to restart it. He said: "The goal here is not to connect my printer." A failing real printer is the test case for the agent's help, so do not repair it, explain it or wait for it before testing.
47	
48	He also said I keep writing "its line was wrong" for lines I wrote. Say "I wrote it" and say why. My likely reason for "add no cause": a false statement is a failure I could see and test for, and a stuck person was not, so I kept the "false" half of his test and dropped the "a person stuck" half.
49	
50	**How to apply:** when a chat goes wrong, read what the person was told before touching a line of it. Do not answer with a patch for the failing line; ask what stopped the model reasoning. The evidence rule in [[connection-skill-per-connection-type]] now covers facts the skill states; guesses are allowed when labelled. See [[bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code]], [[tool-result-states-method]], [[trace-a-rule-to-kenneths-words]].
51	
52	=== tool-result-states-method.md ===
53	---
54	name: tool-result-states-method
55	description: "2026-11-01/02 tool-result sweep: Kenneth's test for a result bug (a person stuck: told something false, right step hidden, cost beyond one call); how the problem statement drifted into 'every distinguishable state' and eight of nine fixes were taken out; branch claude/tool-results-truth"
56	metadata:
57	  node_type: memory
58	  type: feedback
59	  originSessionId: b2d2c400-439c-4486-af2f-1479f86f533d
60	  modified: 2026-11-02T12:51:30.620Z
61	---
62	
63	After the P1S cloud-mode incident (2026-10-31) a code-reading sweep listed eleven tools whose result said less than the app knew, and I fixed nine of them on `claude/tool-silent-failures` (common branch `claude/tool-results-truth`). On 2026-11-02 Kenneth asked why, and eight came out again.
64	
65	**Kenneth's test for a tool-result bug:** a person who plausibly exists, told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call. "Fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem." The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call is not a stuck person. The three that passed: a wrong Bambu access code read as a vanished printer; a print host that answered read as unreachable; a heard printer hidden from the connection (same loop as the incident).
66	
67	**How the statement drifted:** incident (a person stuck, false reason, right step hidden) → sweep ("a tool says less than the app knew", a code shape, eleven matches by reading) → brief ("a class of bug", method + guard, "reproduce before fixing") → my reading (reproduce = make two states read the same over MCP, a property of the code). Each hand-off made it easier to satisfy. The hidden-preset "fix" was the clearest non-problem: no person, the sweep itself said "may be intended".
68	
69	**Why:** the P1S failure was real because you were on the wrong side of it for an evening; the other ten shared its code shape, not its substance. Every field added for a non-problem is text every model reads on every call.
70	
71	**How to apply:** before fixing a result, write the scenario in Kenneth's terms (who, doing what, told what, losing what, which step is hidden); if it cannot be written, it is not a problem, whatever the code looks like. When a brief says "reproduce", ask whether it means "find the case a person hit" (it does, [[reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes]]) before accepting a weaker reading, and raise the gap on receipt, not when asked three times. A rule or guard is worth keeping when it would fail on the real incident; a document nobody reads is not ([[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]] still stands). Kept guards: `test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", harness `*_are_told_apart`, `FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, `StandInHost(hold, answer, status, body)`. Seam: one line in `GUI_App.cpp`'s local-connect CallAfter → `Printers::record_connection_event`; upstream/main added a log line at the same spot, resolve by keeping both.
72	
73	=== forward-the-real-error-four-rules.md ===
74	---
75	name: forward-the-real-error-four-rules
76	description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's method for false tool results: forward what the source gave, else say what the code tested; no new checks; no OrcaSlicer files; applied to sweep entries 1-43 as 469ecf0f8a and b87ab789ca"
77	metadata:
78	  node_type: memory
79	  type: feedback
80	  originSessionId: b47f90f4-7491-4a9c-a16a-eddb38284f24
81	  modified: 2026-11-02T20:28:22.151Z
82	---
83	
84	On 2026-11-02 a sweep listed 71 places where a tool result hid or replaced the real failure. I offered "separate checks" for failures with several causes and said each removed claim "needs a check of what's true". Kenneth called that out: separate checks to tell causes apart are the thing we are trying not to do, and if the code knows nothing, there is nothing to check. He approved four rules for entries 1-43:
85	
86	1. If the source gives an error, forward it.
87	2. If it gives nothing, say what the code tested or saw, and delete any guessed cause. No new checks or branches.
88	3. If a comment says a lower layer's message misleads the model, keep our replacement. Example: `generate_calibration` drops the over-the-build-volume load report on purpose.
89	4. If the fix needs an OrcaSlicer file, skip the entry. Kenneth approves any upstream change one by one.
90	
91	He also waived per-entry reproduction for this batch only. It does not replace the global "reproduce before fixing" rule for other bugs.
92	
93	**Why:** the fix is mechanical once it is seen as forwarding. Inventing a way to classify causes is over-engineering, and it was the earlier reading of "reproduce" that made eight sweep fixes come out again ([[tool-result-states-method]]).
94	
95	**How to apply:**
96	- Before proposing work on a tool result, ask what the source already gives. Say "forward" or "delete the claim", and propose no new check.
97	- A forwarded error reaches the model, so it must not name Orca: `wording.test.ts` does not see those strings. Two throws in `ProjectAutosave.cpp` had to change.
98	- False successes are the exception, because the source gives nothing to forward: `store_stl` always returns true, `export_current_configs` lists unwritten files, `Plater::split_object` returns nothing and only shows a modal, and `ModelObject::split` on a multi-volume object splits only by volume.
99	- Before a force-push or squash on `claude/tool-results-truth`, say a push already happened. Kenneth dropped a squash once he heard it needed one. Pushing to origin needs his word, not my note that it is the process.
100	
101	Left on the list after these commits: entries 44-71, except 47, 48 and 49. Related: [[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]], [[tool-error-contract]].
102	
103	=== rare-failures-get-a-generic-error.md ===
104	---
105	name: rare-failures-get-a-generic-error
106	description: "Kenneth 2026-10-15 — rare, speculative failure paths (save failures etc.) get one generic error; don't design per-cause handling, retries or prompt rules for them"

131	Kenneth settled this on 2026-09-23. In the printer setup flow, "connect your printer" is user wording. For the code it means: find or enter the printer's connection details, check that they work, and save them with that printer. The check may open a real connection for a moment. Setup does NOT promise that the connection stays active after a later printer-profile change.
132

To do that it added an app-wide override to OrcaSlicer's `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent()` (10 upstream lines). The coding agent that wrote it later agreed it had invented that requirement. On jusprin-newui, 264d6f8141 removes the override and bd8ea51abc adds the harness checks. With it gone, selecting a non-Bambu profile gives the connection software back to Orca's profile-driven choice, the same as stock Orca.
134	
135	**How to apply:**
136	- Don't add code that keeps a printer connection alive across profile changes unless Kenneth asks for that behavior explicitly.
137	- After the connection software changes, printer status stays "connected" for up to 30 seconds. That is the normal freshness window in `has_recent_printer_data`, the same one that applies when a printer is switched off. It is not a regression.

160	name: bambu-code-minus-one-not-wrong-code
161	description: "Plug-in code -1 on Kenneth's P1S came with the correct access code while the network was very slow; a direct MQTT login separates a wrong code (rc 5) from a right one (rc 0)"
162	metadata:
163	  node_type: memory
164	  type: project
165	  originSessionId: 445726c4-adce-47cb-81a4-658405e48110
166	  modified: 2026-11-02T20:40:28.093Z
167	---
168	
169	2026-11-02, Kenneth's P1S at 192.168.0.198 in LAN mode, plug-in 02.03.00.62. The real access code gave `ConnectStatusFailed` msg `-1` twice, about 24 s after `set_selected_machine`, the same as a made-up code. A one-off MQTT login to port 8883 (user `bblp`, 60 s timeout) answered CONNACK 0 with the real code and CONNACK 5 with a made-up one, so the code was right and the printer does tell them apart. During those failures TCP 8883 timed out for over a minute. An idle ping showed 64% loss and 15-50 s round trips, while the router answered in 3 ms and other Wi-Fi devices on the network were also slow.
170	
171	Later on 2026-11-02, a saved LAN record at an address with no device at all (TCP 8883: "Host is down") also got `-1`, 12 s after selecting it, and the app's note said "refused". So -1 means at least "no connection made"; it does not need a printer to answer.
172	
173	Correction, 2026-11-02 12:12: I blamed Kenneth's slow Wi-Fi, and a weak signal now looks unlikely. With no app running, about 3 hours after the last connection attempt from my tests, the printer lost 35% of pings at 9.6 s average while the router answered in 3 ms with no loss, and the printer reported -41 dBm and IDLE. A direct login with the right code was accepted but took 27.7 s, 26 s of it setting up TLS, which is longer than the ~24 s after which the plug-in reports -1. My hypothesis, unverified: on a slow printer the plug-in gives up before the code is tested. The cause of the slowness is unknown. Finding it is not the goal: see [[connection-skill-explains-not-lookup]].
174	
175	**Why:** the app's note said "The printer refused the connection" until commit 35fed2c439 and its follow-up, and the skill's `failed` line tells the model to have the person compare the code. For this person both were false and hid the real problem. My hypothesis, unverified: -1 is the plug-in's timeout, and on a healthy network a wrong code gives another answer, perhaps the `5` upstream handles.
176	
177	**How to apply:** before concluding anything from a connect failure, check that the printer answers on TCP 8883 in under a second; `--printer-live-p1s <address> real-code` takes the code from `JUSPRIN_P1S_CODE`. A failure during a slow spell says nothing about the code. See [[printer-network-check-harness]] and [[connection-skill-per-connection-type]].

206	
207	Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.
208	
209	**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.
210	
211	**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.
212	
213	**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.
214	
215	**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".
216	
217	**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). # Computer use (desktop control)

Computer use lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling, through the Claude desktop app. Its tools are named `mcp__computer-use__*` (for example `request_access`, `screenshot`) when the session runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` (for example `computer_request_access`, `computer_screenshot`) when the session runs in the cloud and is linked to the person's computer. Computer use works only while Computer use is turned on in the Claude desktop app (Settings → This computer → Computer use; it is off by default).

## Turning computer use on from a chat

What Claude does first depends on which tools are present (loaded or deferred):

1. **Computer-use tools are present.** Claude goes straight to the access flow below.
2. **No computer-use tools, but an `enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer` tool is present.** Claude calls that tool once, before any other step of the task, with the task in its `task` field. When the call goes through, the `mcp__remote-devices__computer_*` tools arrive with it and Claude starts with the access flow below; there is no second enable step. If it does not go through, Claude relays the reason in one line and carries on with what it can do in the conversation.
3. **Neither.** Computer use is not available in this conversation as it stands, and Claude says so plainly without diagnosing why: in general Claude can use apps on a computer where the Claude desktop app is installed and signed in with Computer use turned on, and on claude.ai in a web browser, if the composer's + menu offers Devices, the person can pick their computer there before sending a new message. Claude does not pretend to act.

## Separate filesystems

Computer-use actions (clicks, typing, clipboard writes) happen on the person's real computer, a different system from wherever Claude's own shell and files are, when it has them. Files Claude creates on its side do not exist on the person's machine. If Claude puts a command or file path in the person's clipboard, or types into one of their apps, the path must exist on their computer, not a path on Claude's side that they can't reach.

- **A Moonraker or OctoPrint printer** never announces itself. The model has to ask the person for its address before anything can run. The app only knows which kind it is once printer_connect names it, and only then does it add that skill.

Each first step happens before any skill has been added, so the prompt is the only place it can live. Everything after the first step is in the skills.

64	
65	## What the search found
66	- **Bambu's own documentation:** its [network ports page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/printer-network-ports) lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, by SSDP (a standard way for devices to announce themselves) over multicast or broadcast, in both cloud and LAN mode. 67	- **Community reports, not official:**
68	  - [One person's capture](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Schaefer/72a9e2491a42da2ef99fb87601955cc3) of a P1S in LAN mode shows a packet every 5 seconds, with the destination alternating between 1990 and 2021. That would put one on port 2021 every 10 seconds.
69	  - A [forum thread](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/use-ssdp-standards/7173) confirms the non-standard ports, but nobody there measured the timing and no Bambu staff replied.
70	- **Wi-Fi in general:** [an IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-mboned-ieee802-mcast-problems-00) says multicast over Wi-Fi isn't acknowledged or resent, so packets can simply be lost. Whether that causes our delays is my hypothesis; I haven't tested it.

146	The notes say `start_discovery`'s second argument makes the plug-in also send M-SEARCH. JusPrin passes `false`, as Bambu Studio does at startup, so the app only listens and waits. 149	This replaces the hour-long listen and the 10 repeated runs:
150	1. **Run one packet capture beside one no-model check.** That shows directly whether the announcements reached the Mac and the app missed them, or never arrived. A capture running during the 08:57 miss would have answered that.
151	2. **Send one M-SEARCH from a small script** and see whether the P1S replies, and how fast. It's only a query and changes nothing on the printer.
152	3. **Look at how long the wait should be only if a question remains after that.**
153	
154	Both need the Mac back on the printer's network. The capture also needs admin rights, which this session doesn't have, so you'd start it yourself in a terminal when we're ready:
155	
156	```bash
157	sudo tcpdump -i en0 -n -tttt -w /tmp/p1s-capture.pcap 'udp and host 192.168.0.198'
158	```

167	
168	## The order I should follow
169	1. **Name the one question,** and what answer would change my next step. Here it was "where does the delay happen?", not "how long should the wait be?". I jumped to tuning a number before knowing what the number was compensating for.
170	2. **Ask who already knows:** documentation, other people's code, issue trackers, the binary itself.
171	3. **Check what we've already recorded:** logs and earlier runs. Your log had 1,195 lines waiting.

I still didn't follow them, so another written rule alone is unlikely to fix this. What pulled me along was having a harness ready and a clear task to run it, so doing the next step felt like progress.

I hadn't searched before asking you to decide; I have now. I'm withdrawing the 45-second suggestion and the decision I put to you. Bambu documents which ports printers announce on, but I found no published timing for how often. I also still don't have a usable measurement, because this Mac left the printer's network before my 10-minute listen started.

## What the search found
- **Bambu's own documentation:** its [network ports page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/printer-network-ports) lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, by SSDP (a standard way for devices to announce themselves) over multicast or broadcast, in both cloud and LAN mode. I only saw this through a search result, because fetching the page directly returned an error. I found no published interval or description of the process.
- **Community reports, not official:**
  - [One person's capture](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Schaefer/72a9e2491a42da2ef99fb87601955cc3) of a P1S in LAN mode shows a packet every 5 seconds, with the destination alternating between 1990 and 2021. That would put one on port 2021 every 10 seconds.
  - A [forum thread](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/use-ssdp-standards/7173) confirms the non-standard ports, but nobody there measured the timing and no Bambu staff replied.
- **Wi-Fi in general:** [an IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-mboned-ieee802-mcast-problems-00) says multicast over Wi-Fi isn't acknowledged or resent, so packets can simply be lost. Whether that causes our delays is my hypothesis; I haven't tested it.

## What I measured
| Measurement | Result | What it's worth |
|---|---|---|
| 30-second listen | Announcements at 19.2 s and 29.1 s | The 9.9 s gap fits the 10-second report, but it's only one gap |
| Time for the app to first hear the printer | 14, 21, 25, 25 and 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31 | Six samples |
| One no-model run at about 08:57 | Heard nothing for 120 s | Unexplained |
| 10-minute listen from about 10:37 | Zero packets | **Void** |

The void listen wasn't caught until afterwards. The Mac slept with its lid closed at 10:14, woke at 10:35, and is now on `192.168.15.221` instead of the printer's `192.168.0.x` network.

## What this does and doesn't tell us
- **The timing doesn't add up yet:** if port 2021 really gets a packet every 10 seconds, the app should hear the printer within about 10 seconds. It usually took longer, and once it heard nothing for two minutes. So something else is going on, and I don't know what.
- **Where the delay could be:** the app code I read passes each announcement straight through, though I only read part of that path. That leaves the printer, the Wi-Fi or Bambu's plug-in, which ships as a compiled library in the plugins folder, so I can't read its logic.
- **The dark screen:** I said waking it made no visible difference, but that was one chat against one chat, which isn't enough to say either way.

## What I'll do next
The next step is a free measurement that sends nothing to the printer and uses no live model. It needs the Mac back on the printer's network.
1. Listen passively for about an hour and record every gap between announcements on both ports, confirming before and after that the Mac stayed on that network.
2. Run the no-model check about 10 times to see how often and how quickly the app hears the printer, and how often it misses.
3. Compare the two. If the printer sends steadily but the app hears it late, the delay is on the Mac or plug-in side. If the gaps themselves are irregular, it's the printer or the Wi-Fi.

Until then the search wait stays at 15 seconds, and the two false statements the model made are still unfixed:
- "The search stops after about 15 seconds."
- "I couldn't find your P1S", said shortly before the printer was heard.

Nothing is committed since `5f3bd2e59a`. These findings are in `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md` in the worktree root, untracked, with a copy in the shared notes folder.

- **Printer chat:** it receives no skills at all (`App.tsx` skips sending them).
- **Choosing the skill:** the earlier skills branches failed partly because the model had to pick the right one.

So I'd use the same file format, with these changes:

1. **One note per printer model:** each claim carries its source, status and last confirmed firmware. A model drafts the first version from public sources.
2. **The app supplies the note:** it knows which printer is being discussed, so the model doesn't have to choose.
3. **The app records outcomes:** if the printer connected after the note was shown, that counts as evidence without relying on the model's opinion.
4. **Corrections stay local first:** when a person says "that menu isn't there", the model drafts an edit and the person approves it. It applies to their own copy straight away, which is the self-correcting part.
5. **That edit becomes the report:** the person previews it with access codes and serials removed, then presses send. A bot turns it into a draft pull request, and a person merges it.

descriptions, which every printer chat reads, including chats that only pick a
profile. They now live in skill files under AgentUI/src/skills/: connect-bambu,
connect-moonraker (Klipper printers) and connect-octoprint. The tools say only

tells the causes of a failure apart, instead of listing one next step per
state. An earlier version did that and sent a person back to re-check a
correct code, because the plug-in's code -1 came with a wrong code, with the
right code and with an address that has no printer.

When a skill is added: the app adds it to the conversation, once, the first
time the person tries to connect (a chat opened to connect, a
printer_connection_status or printer_connect call on a saved printer, or the
printer form finished with a printer found on the network). The app picks it
from the connection type; the model never chooses it. For a print host the
type is known from the saved connection or from the first printer_connect's
hostType, and before that neither host skill is sent, because a skill stays in
the chat once sent. That is why AgentSkillUse gains `stays`. The printer
panel's page did not send skills to the app before, so it does now.

a guess, ask for the cheapest check, and do not repeat a failed step unless
something changed. A failed connection note reports what the app saw: the
plug-in's code, how long it took, and a TCP look at port 8883 just before the

---
name: connect-bambu
trigger: connect_bambu
---

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The app's note then says the connection is verified.

## What the tools report

Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- `started` or `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty means nothing has been heard so far, which is silence and not a finding. The search goes on. After `started`, say you are looking and end your message: the app posts a note when a printer appears, or after about 15 seconds with none, and starts your next turn. Reading the status again before then shows nothing new.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `credential_requested` means the form is up. Say to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again, which opens the form.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

=== OCTOPRINT ===

name: connect-octoprint
trigger: connect_octoprint
---

# Connecting a printer through OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through its web page in a browser. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.
2. **The person gives the address they open OctoPrint at.** It can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up gets no answer at all.
3. **The person types an API key into the app's form.** The OctoPrint tried here answered without a key as well, but only to refuse: HTTP 403, "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. You have not seen OctoPrint's settings, so search for where their version shows the key before you say, and ask what they see.
4. **The app asks OctoPrint for its version.** The app's note then says the connection is verified. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen against a real OctoPrint, or against the same network failures with a Moonraker:

- **HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission…".** OctoPrint answered and got no key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 403 "Invalid API key".** OctoPrint answered and refused the key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as OctoPrint answers. This came when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint, and when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, so a Klipper printer with Mainsail or Fluidd may be what they have.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or OctoPrint may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a server that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the OctoPrint computer and this one are on the same network, or restarting OctoPrint. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again with the address to use.

I also still don't have a usable measurement, because this Mac left the printer's network before my 10-minute listen started.
64	
65	## What the search found
66	- **Bambu's own documentation:** its [network ports page](https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/general/printer-network-ports) lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, by SSDP (a standard way for devices to announce themselves) over multicast or broadcast, in both cloud and LAN mode. I only saw this through a search result, because fetching the page directly returned an error. I found no published interval or description of the process.
67	- **Community reports, not official:**
68	  - [One person's capture](https://gist.github.com/Alex-Schaefer/72a9e2491a42da2ef99fb87601955cc3) of a P1S in LAN mode shows a packet every 5 seconds, with the destination alternating between 1990 and 2021. That would put one on port 2021 every 10 seconds.
69	  - A [forum thread](https://forum.bambulab.com/t/use-ssdp-standards/7173) confirms the non-standard ports, but nobody there measured the timing and no Bambu staff replied.
70	- **Wi-Fi in general:** [an IETF draft](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-mboned-ieee802-mcast-problems-00) says multicast over Wi-Fi isn't acknowledged or resent, so packets can simply be lost. Whether that causes our delays is my hypothesis; I haven't tested it.
71	
72	## What I measured
73	| Measurement | Result | What it's worth |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| 30-second listen | Announcements at 19.2 s and 29.1 s | The 9.9 s gap fits the 10-second report, but it's only one gap |
76	| Time for the app to first hear the printer | 14, 21, 25, 25 and 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31 | Six samples |
77	| One no-model run at about 08:57 | Heard nothing for 120 s | Unexplained |
78	| 10-minute listen from about 10:37 | Zero packets | **Void** |
79	
80	The void listen wasn't caught until afterwards. The Mac slept with its lid closed at 10:14, woke at 10:35, and is now on `192.168.15.221` instead of the printer's `192.168.0.x` network.
81	
82	## What this does and doesn't tell us
83	- **The timing doesn't add up yet:** if port 2021 really gets a packet every 10 seconds, the app should hear the printer within about 10 seconds. It usually took longer, and once it heard nothing for two minutes. So something else is going on, and I don't know what.
84	- **Where the delay could be:** the app code I read passes each announcement straight through, though I only read part of that path. That leaves the printer, the Wi-Fi or Bambu's plug-in, which ships as a compiled library in the plugins folder, so I can't read its logic.
85	- **The dark screen:** I said waking it made no visible difference, but that was one chat against one chat, which isn't enough to say either way.

Add connection skills to the printer chat for Bambu, Moonraker and OctoPrint

The steps for connecting a printer lived in the two connection tools'
descriptions, which every printer chat reads, including chats that only pick a
profile. They now live in skill files under AgentUI/src/skills/: connect-bambu,
connect-moonraker (Klipper printers) and connect-octoprint. The tools say only
what each state means; each skill explains how that connection works and what
tells the causes of a failure apart, instead of listing one next step per
state. An earlier version did that and sent a person back to re-check a
correct code, because the plug-in's code -1 came with a wrong code, with the
right code and with an address that has no printer.

When a skill is added: the app adds it to the conversation, once, the first
time the person tries to connect (a chat opened to connect, a
printer_connection_status or printer_connect call on a saved printer, or the
printer form finished with a printer found on the network). The app picks it
from the connection type; the model never chooses it. For a print host the
type is known from the saved connection or from the first printer_connect's
hostType, and before that neither host skill is sent, because a skill stays in
the chat once sent. That is why AgentSkillUse gains `stays`. The printer
panel's page did not send skills to the app before, so it does now.

The printer prompt's connecting rule says to call printer_connection_status
for a Bambu printer "once the person wants to connect". Worded as "start with
printer_connection_status", it made the model check the network right after
adding a printer instead of offering to connect: 4 of 18 runs of
add-then-undo and add-named-model on DeepSeek V4 Flash, against none of 18
with either the old sentence or the old status description put back, and
none of 12 with this wording.

The printer prompt holds one way of working: give the likeliest explanation as
a guess, ask for the cheapest check, and do not repeat a failed step unless
something changed. A failed connection note reports what the app saw: the

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen.
4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
5. **The printer sends its status.** The app's note then says the connection is verified.

## What the tools report

Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.

- `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
- `started` or `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty means nothing has been heard so far, which is silence and not a finding. The search goes on. After `started`, say you are looking and end your message: the app posts a note when a printer appears, or after about 15 seconds with none, and starts your next turn. Reading the status again before then shows nothing new.
- `port_taken` means another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, which may be another slicer, so nothing can be heard whatever the printer is doing. `not_listening` means this app is not listening and takes that port only as it starts. Both need a restart of this app, the first after closing the other one.
- `candidates` lists printers the app knows in LAN mode, heard on the network or saved from an earlier connection. Only an attempt shows whether one answers. With one, if they have asked to connect, call `printer_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `credential_requested` means the form is up. Say to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note.
- `cloud_mode` means the printer was heard with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until that is on. Say so with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way.
- `linked_elsewhere` means this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. The way forward is Connect… in that printer's menu on Home.
- `unknown_device` means `printer_connect` refused the name it was given, and its message says why. When no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`.
- `unavailable` means it cannot connect, and `message` says why. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows a notice with an Install button under the message. Wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again. The search is `not_started` then, and says nothing about the printer.

## When a connection fails

A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:

- **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
- **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.
- **It answered both times.** The network reached the printer, so suspect the login, and a mistyped code is the likeliest. This has not been seen on a real printer, so it is a guess too. Owners on Bambu's forum report that the code changes when LAN Only is switched off and on, so an older code may no longer be right.
- **It turned the connection down at once.** The printer is reachable but not taking logins. This has not been seen on a real printer. A printer that is still starting up is one guess.

What is worth trying for the network or the printer has not been tested on this printer, so search for what owners of this model report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: wait a few minutes, restart the printer, ask what its screen shows about Wi-Fi signal, or bring it closer to the router. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again, which opens the form.

## When they are stuck

The JusPrin developers can only fix what they hear about, and they have not tested most printers. A person who has tried and wants them to know can report it with `issue_report_open`, which opens a GitHub issue page in their browser with your summary filled in. It files nothing: they read the page, change it if they like, and submit it with their own GitHub account.

# Connecting a printer through OctoPrint

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.

## How the connection works

Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing about the ones after it.

1. **OctoPrint runs on a computer beside the printer and drives it.** People use it through its web page in a browser. The app talks only to OctoPrint, never to the printer itself.
2. **The person gives the address they open OctoPrint at.** It can be an IP address or a name, but a name this computer cannot look up gets no answer at all.
3. **The person types an API key into the app's form.** The OctoPrint tried here answered without a key as well, but only to refuse: HTTP 403, "You don't have the permission to access the requested resource". A wrong key got HTTP 403 "Invalid API key", so the two can be told apart. You have not seen OctoPrint's settings, so search for where their version shows the key before you say, and ask what they see.
4. **The app asks OctoPrint for its version.** The app's note then says the connection is verified. That means OctoPrint answered and took the key, and nothing more: it answered the same way with no printer attached to it.

## What the tools report

- `not_configured` means no connection has been saved yet. `unknown` means one is saved and has not been tested in this chat.
- `failed` comes with what the app's test was told, in the host's own words where it gave any.

## When a connection fails

What the test was told says which step to suspect. Each of these was seen against a real OctoPrint, or against the same network failures with a Moonraker:

- **HTTP 403 "You don't have the permission…".** OctoPrint answered and got no key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 403 "Invalid API key".** OctoPrint answered and refused the key. The address is right.
- **HTTP 404.** Something answered at that address, but not as OctoPrint answers. This came when Moonraker was chosen for an OctoPrint, and when OctoPrint was chosen for a Moonraker, so a Klipper printer with Mainsail or Fluidd may be what they have.
- **"Connection refused".** The machine at that address answered at once, but nothing was listening on that port. The port may be wrong, or OctoPrint may not be running.
- **"Connection timed out", after about 10 seconds.** Nothing answered. This came from an address with no device on it, and also from `https://` in front of a server that speaks plain `http://`, so despite what the message says about the network, an `https://` address is worth trying with `http://` first.
- **No answer after 30 seconds.** The test was still waiting. This came from a name ending in `.local` that no device answered to. The IP address avoids looking up the name.

What is worth trying beyond this has not been tested here, so search for what people with the same setup report before you suggest it. Without a search, general knowledge gives: opening the same address in a browser on this computer, checking the OctoPrint computer and this one are on the same network, or restarting OctoPrint. When they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again with the address to use.
